label: Lagrangian Mechanics on Manifolds
notes: This chapter lifts Lagrangian mechanics off the flat coordinate plane and onto a smooth configuration manifold. We motivate why constrained systems, like a pendulum or a rigid body, force us to think intrinsically rather than in ambient coordinates. Preview the four pillars: the manifold, its tangent bundle, the Lagrangian, and Noether's theorem.

label: Configuration Manifold
notes: Introduce the configuration manifold M as the set of all positions the system can occupy. The pendulum lives on a circle, a planar double pendulum on a torus. Stress that a chart gives generalized coordinates, but the manifold itself is the coordinate-free object. The dimension of M is the number of degrees of freedom.

label: Tangent Bundle TM
notes: Velocities are not points of M but tangent vectors. Assemble all tangent spaces into the tangent bundle TM, whose points are pairs of a position and a velocity. This 2n-dimensional manifold is the true state space of Lagrangian mechanics. Emphasize that a motion is a curve in M, and its lift to TM records velocity at each instant.

label: The Lagrangian on TM
notes: Define the Lagrangian as a smooth function on the tangent bundle, possibly time dependent. In local coordinates it reads L of q, q-dot, t. Stress that L assigns a number to each state, and that the whole of mechanics will be derived from a single variational principle applied to this one function.

label: Euler-Lagrange Equations
notes: State Hamilton's principle of stationary action and derive the Euler-Lagrange equations. Emphasize that although written in coordinates, the equations transform correctly between charts, so they define an intrinsic second-order system on TM. This coordinate independence is exactly what lets us work on a manifold.

label: Holonomic Constraints
notes: Explain holonomic constraints as smooth equations on configurations that cut out a submanifold. The constrained configuration space is that submanifold, of lower dimension. Constrained Lagrangian mechanics is just ordinary Lagrangian mechanics on the submanifold, using the restricted Lagrangian. Contrast briefly with non-holonomic constraints, which are not treated this way.

label: Kinetic Energy as a Metric
notes: Show that kinetic energy is a positive-definite quadratic form in the velocities, hence a Riemannian metric on M. The mass matrix is the metric in coordinates. Free motion becomes geodesic motion. Emphasize that geometry is not imposed from outside; the kinetic energy itself supplies the metric of configuration space.

label: Natural Systems L = T - U
notes: Define a natural mechanical system by L equals kinetic minus potential energy. Write the Euler-Lagrange equations in this case and recover Newton's law with the metric connection. Stress that the potential bends trajectories away from geodesics, and that energy T plus U is conserved when L has no explicit time dependence.

label: Symmetries and First Integrals
notes: Introduce one-parameter groups of diffeomorphisms of M and what it means for the Lagrangian to be invariant under such a group. Build intuition with a rotationally symmetric potential. A symmetry is a continuous transformation that leaves the physics unchanged, and this invariance is about to yield a conserved quantity.

label: Noether's Theorem
notes: State Noether's theorem precisely: invariance of the Lagrangian under a one-parameter group generated by a vector field X gives a first integral, the pairing of the momentum with X. Stress the construction is coordinate free and that the conserved quantity is read off directly from the generating vector field of the symmetry.

label: Rotation Gives Angular Momentum
notes: Work the canonical example: rotational symmetry of an isotropic system yields conservation of angular momentum. Trace through how the rotation vector field pairs with the kinetic momentum to produce the conserved component. This is the concrete payoff of Noether and connects symmetry directly to the classical conservation laws students already know.

label: Synthesis and Outlook
notes: Recap the dictionary: configuration manifold, tangent bundle as state space, Lagrangian as a function on TM, Euler-Lagrange as an intrinsic flow, kinetic energy as metric, and Noether linking symmetry to conservation. Point forward to the Legendre transform and the cotangent bundle, where Hamiltonian mechanics and symplectic geometry take over.
